correctness.rationale: The frozen exact count is correct, but not new. In the truncated algebra every maximal-ideal element has p-th power zero. Lifts e(x_i) on the image tangent block and x_j-e(x_j) on its complement have invertible linear part and conjugate the idempotent to the coordinate map. The centralizer has the two invertible diagonal blocks and the stated independent higher-degree coefficient choices. The repaired theorem uses the identical known count directly. On writing b=d-k, the exponent is p^d h_d(b)-b(d-b+1) with h_d(b)=d-b-(d-2b)p^(-b). The Gaussian coefficient contributes between zero and d^2 to the base-q log. The adjacent difference is -1+((p-1)(d-2b)+2)/p^(b+1); below floor(log_p d)-1 it is at least 1/2 for large d, and from floor(log_p d)+1 onward at most -1/(2p). Each exterior stratum therefore loses a uniform positive multiple of p^d in log mass to an endpoint stratum, uniformly dominating the O(d^2) log error. Summing over at most d+1 terms gives the repaired probability bound. On the window, d p^(-B_d) is between 1/p and p^2, as claimed. No finite check is needed for the limit; the included script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Uniform on idempotent coefficient-fixing maps, not uniform on isomorphism classes or embedded images; fixed p and q.

value.rationale: The surviving claim answers a natural distributional question about a standard finite local algebra: a typical map discards only logarithmically many generators, yet its image dimension is down by a factor of order d. Locating the integer ambiguity in a genuine three-index window uses adjacent ratios and compares all ranks, not an arbitrary small-parameter test or a rephrasing of the prior count. The exact enumeration is a useful input, not the asserted advance.
residual_risks: No relative weights within the window, joint field/dimension growth, or distribution on embedded images claimed.
